sources.entry: Checklist - The A11Y Project for accessibility

summary.title: Checklist - The A11Y Project
summary.one_liner: A practical web accessibility checklist, organized by area (content, keyboard, images, forms, media, color, mobile), with each item mapped to a WCAG success criterion.
keywords: wcag conformance levels a aa aaa
takeaways: WCAG has three conformance levels (A, AA, AAA); the A11Y Project aims for AA.
Use semantic HTML: a and button elements, lang and title attributes, landmarks, one h1, ordered headings, lists and tables with th and caption.
Give images meaningful alt text, and use empty alt for decorative images.
Make forms accessible with label/for pairing, fieldset and legend, error summaries, and non-color-only state indicators.
No checklist makes a site perfectly accessible; periodic testing and professional help are recommended.
summary.summary: This is a web accessibility checklist from The A11Y Project that uses WCAG as its reference and explains the A, AA and AAA levels. It lists practical checks grouped into sections: content, global code, keyboard, images, headings, lists, controls, tables, forms, media, appearance, animation, color contrast, and mobile/touch. Each item gives a short, actionable rule with a rationale and often the related WCAG success criterion. It also states that the checklist does not guarantee accessibility and suggests professional testing.
